key_insight: Hard-carbon microstructure controls whether Na+ merely penetrates briefly or sustains transport, with lower-density, more open structures enabling deeper and more persistent ion motion.
engineering_relevance: Designing hard carbon anodes with tailored pore accessibility and ordering can improve sodium storage kinetics and help optimize high-density electrodes that still charge effectively.
method: Machine-learning-generated hard-carbon structures spanning 0.5–2.0 g cm-3
Molecular dynamics with explicit 1 M NaPF6 in EC/DMC electrolyte
3D trajectory and potential-of-mean-force analyses of Na+ penetration and transport
evidence_signal: The simulations show that Na+ uptake increases with applied potential but drops strongly as carbon density rises, even though the densest structure still exhibits electrode charging.
watch_item: Deep penetration depth does not guarantee sustained transport, so pore accessibility and retention must be evaluated separately from transient ion entry.
paper_title: Distinguishing sodium-ion penetration and sustained transport in realistic hard carbon nanostructures
